c01.display: Welcome back to NLP, Simply Explained. This is unit 5, lesson 2, our final lesson: BERT.
c01.spoken: Welcome back to N L P, Simply Explained. This is unit 5, lesson 2, our final lesson: BERT.

c02.display: ELMo showed that pretraining on plain text pays off. BERT took that idea and changed NLP almost overnight.
c02.spoken: ELMo showed that pretraining on plain text pays off. BERT took that idea and changed N L P almost overnight.

c03.display: Here's the idea. BERT learned language by filling in blanks, millions and millions of times, reading in both directions at once.
c03.spoken: Here's the idea. BERT learned language by filling in blanks, millions and millions of times, reading in both directions at once.

c04.display: BERT, from 2018, stands for bidirectional encoder representations from transformers. It's a model pretrained on lots of text, to understand every word in its full context.
c04.spoken: BERT, from 2018, stands for bidirectional encoder representations from transformers. It's a model pretrained on lots of text, to understand every word in its full context.

c05.display: Show it "she sat on the blank of the river", and it fills in: bank.
c05.spoken: Show it "she sat on the blank of the river", and it fills in: bank.

c06.display: Think of a student who has done millions of fill-in-the-blank exercises, and only then specialises for one particular exam.
c06.spoken: Think of a student who has done millions of fill-in-the-blank exercises, and only then specialises for one particular exam.

c07.display: BERT is built from a Transformer, and its key ingredient is self-attention. Every word looks at every other word in the sentence, and decides which ones matter for its meaning.
c07.spoken: BERT is built from a Transformer, and its key ingredient is self-attention. Every word looks at every other word in the sentence, and decides which ones matter for its meaning.

c08.display: In "the cat drank the milk because it was hungry", the word "it" pays most attention to "cat", because hungry things are cats, not milk.
c08.spoken: In "the cat drank the milk because it was hungry", the word "it" pays most attention to "cat", because hungry things are cats, not milk.

c09.display: Think of a meeting where each person listens most closely to the people who are relevant to them.
c09.spoken: Think of a meeting where each person listens most closely to the people who are relevant to them.

c10.display: BERT was pretrained with two simple games, played on books and Wikipedia.
c10.spoken: BERT was pretrained with two simple games, played on books and Wikipedia.

c11.display: Mask: hide about fifteen percent of the words in each passage.
c11.spoken: Mask: hide about fifteen percent of the words in each passage.

c12.display: Predict: guess the hidden words, using the words on both sides. This is called a masked language model.
c12.spoken: Predict: guess the hidden words, using the words on both sides. This is called a masked language model.

c13.display: Next sentence: given two sentences, guess whether the second really follows the first.
c13.spoken: Next sentence: given two sentences, guess whether the second really follows the first.

c14.display: Here are some blanks BERT might fill in.
c14.spoken: Here are some blanks BERT might fill in.

c15.display: "The cat sat on the blank": probably mat.
c15.spoken: "The cat sat on the blank": probably mat.

c16.display: "I drank a cup of blank": tea, or coffee.
c16.spoken: "I drank a cup of blank": tea, or coffee.

c17.display: "Paris is the capital of blank": France. Filling in blanks like these, it picks up grammar, meaning, and a surprising amount of world knowledge.
c17.spoken: "Paris is the capital of blank": France. Filling in blanks like these, it picks up grammar, meaning, and a surprising amount of world knowledge.

c18.display: How do you use BERT for your own task? Four steps.
c18.spoken: How do you use BERT for your own task? Four steps.

c19.display: Pretrain once: this expensive part has already been done for you.
c19.spoken: Pretrain once: this expensive part has already been done for you.

c20.display: Add a layer: put a small extra layer on top, for your task, like spam or not spam.
c20.spoken: Add a layer: put a small extra layer on top, for your task, like spam or not spam.

c21.display: Fine-tune: train the whole thing briefly on your labelled examples. A few thousand is often enough.
c21.spoken: Fine-tune: train the whole thing briefly on your labelled examples. A few thousand is often enough.

c22.display: Use: now it can classify, tag, or answer questions.
c22.spoken: Use: now it can classify, tag, or answer questions.

c23.display: How does BERT compare with ELMo?
c23.spoken: How does BERT compare with ELMo?

c24.display: ELMo uses LSTMs that read each direction separately, and its vectors are fed into your own model.
c24.spoken: ELMo uses L S T ems that read each direction separately, and its vectors are fed into your own model.

c25.display: In BERT, every word sees all the others at once, through self-attention, and the whole model is fine-tuned for your task. When it arrived, it set new records on many language tasks.
c25.spoken: In BERT, every word sees all the others at once, through self-attention, and the whole model is fine-tuned for your task. When it arrived, it set new records on many language tasks.

c26.display: BERT-style models now do many of the jobs we've met in this course.
c26.spoken: BERT-style models now do many of the jobs we've met in this course.

c28.display: Finding the names of people, places and dates.
c28.spoken: Finding the names of people, places and dates.

c29.display: Answering questions from a passage of text.
c29.spoken: Answering questions from a passage of text.

c30.display: And improving search. Google announced in 2019 that it was using BERT to better understand search queries.
c30.spoken: And improving search. Google announced in 2019 that it was using BERT to better understand search queries.

c31.display: Quick quiz. During pretraining, what does BERT's masked language model do?
c31.spoken: Quick quiz. During pretraining, what does BERT's masked language model do?

c33.display: It guesses hidden words, using the words on both sides of the blank.
c33.spoken: It guesses hidden words, using the words on both sides of the blank.

c34.display: Let's recap. BERT learns language by filling in blanks, reading in both directions.
c34.spoken: Let's recap. BERT learns language by filling in blanks, reading in both directions.

c35.display: Self-attention lets every word look at every other word.
c35.spoken: Self-attention lets every word look at every other word.

c36.display: You pretrain once, then fine-tune for your own task.
c36.spoken: You pretrain once, then fine-tune for your own task.

c37.display: And with that, you've climbed the whole staircase, from tokens all the way to BERT. Thanks for learning with NLP, Simply Explained.
c37.spoken: And with that, you've climbed the whole staircase, from tokens all the way to BERT. Thanks for learning with N L P, Simply Explained.
